franchise_profile.description: Optional slug selecting a file under prompts/franchise_profiles/<slug>.md. The file is loaded as a second system message by every agent that has been wired for franchise-aware prompting (plot_architect, prose_stylist, and any agent whose context dict carries franchise_profile_text). Leave unset for original fiction or projects that do not need franchise-specific register/canon rules.

canon_status.description: Canon posture. Canonical enum values only. Use 'canon_status_description' for prose context (e.g., 'post-Fate of the Jedi, 47 ABY').

canon_status_description.description: Optional descriptive phrase elaborating on the canon_status. Use for era/divergence context.

tone.description: Primary tonal register. Use 'tone_description' for descriptive blends that don't fit the enum neatly.

tone_description.description: Optional descriptive phrase elaborating on the tone (e.g., 'Classic Star Wars adventure layered over genuine moral dilemma — personal stakes, tight cast, archaeological mystery building to cosmic crisis').

series.description: Reference to series seed (for planned_series or continuation)

series_id.description: Top-level series ID for shared state across books. Books with the same series_id share story state (characters, arcs, plot threads). Leave empty for standalone books. Also accessible via meta.series.series_id for backward compat.

cosmology_id.description: Optional reference to a cosmology_meta.json at data/cosmologies/<cosmology_id>/. When set, this book's universe belongs to a shared meta-universe (Sanderson-style). Consumed lazily in Phase 2 — engine behaviour with or without this field is identical until a later phase wires cross-universe lore resolution.

branch_point.description: Optional AU divergence metadata, copied from universe_meta.branch_point by the bundle compiler / installer so canon_expert can read it from the concept_seed at runtime. When set, canon_expert reclassifies cross-continuity / era-accuracy violations that relate to facts past the declared divergence_point as 'post_divergence_drift' with reduced severity rather than 'critical'. Descriptive when absent.

source_canon.description: Name of the canon this universe diverges from (e.g., 'Star Wars Legends EU', 'Tolkien Middle-earth').

divergence_point.description: When/where the divergence occurs (e.g., 'post-Lost Tribe crisis, circa 44 ABY').

divergence_description.description: Narrative description of how this universe differs from source canon from the divergence point forward.

protagonist_arc_type.description: Top-level classification of the protagonist's arc. Per-character structured arc classification lives under ensemble_cast[].weiland_arc.arc_type.

voice_notes.description: Per-character voice guidance. Deprecated in favour of voice_definition.character_voices (post-Phase-5); retained for backward compatibility with Phase 5 seeds.

arc_type.description: Weiland arc type — canonical enum only. Use 'arc_summary' for the descriptive phrase. Negative-arc variants: 'disillusionment' = Lie to bleaker Truth; 'corruption' = glimpses Truth, consciously rejects it for Lie; 'fall' = never sees Truth, buried deeper in Lie. Use the bare 'negative' bucket only when the variant is intentionally ambiguous. Use 'supporting_presence' when a character appears in the ensemble cast but is not tracked as a full Weiland arc — their thematic weight lives in presence and contrast, not in lie-breaking progression; when this value is set, lie_believed/ghost/want/need/arc_phase_map may be omitted or held as character texture.

arc_summary.description: Optional descriptive phrase elaborating on the arc (e.g., 'moves from the lie (self-reliance as safety) to the truth (collective trust as strength)'). Complements the strict arc_type enum.

arc_phase_targets.description: Legacy phase-target vocabulary (lie_reinforced/lie_questioned/lie_cracking/lie_confronted/truth_resolved). Retained for backward compatibility. New seeds should prefer 'arc_phase_map' with the 6-phase vocabulary documented on that field.

initial_phase.description: The arc phase this character starts the story in. Defaults to 'lie_established' for all arc types. Must be a valid phase for the character's arc_type.

arc_phase_map.description: Chapter-level map of Weiland arc progression. Keys are phase names; values are chapter references. Canonical vocabularies per arc_type: positive_change / flat use [lie_established, lie_reinforced, lie_challenged, moment_of_truth, new_truth_demonstrated, arc_resolved]; corruption / fall use [lie_established, lie_reinforced, lie_deepened, point_of_no_return, lie_acted_upon, lie_consequence, arc_resolved_tragic]; disillusionment uses [lie_established, lie_reinforced, lie_challenged, truth_glimpsed, bleaker_truth_accepted, arc_resolved_bleak]; static negative (villain flat-lie) uses [lie_established, lie_reinforced, lie_tested, lie_unchanged]. Optional — supporting characters with minor arcs may omit this.

referenced_characters.description: Characters who appear in scene cards but are not in the ensemble cast. Registered with minimal state (no arc tracking). Franchise-agnostic way to prevent 'unknown character' warnings.

relationship_arcs.description: Dyad-level arc planning parallel to ensemble_cast[].weiland_arc. Tracks how each important relationship evolves across the book. Applies Weiland's Lie/Ghost/Want/Need rubric to the relationship itself rather than to an individual character. Optional — only populate for relationships whose evolution is load-bearing for the story.

dyad.description: Character-pair identifier in 'Name/Name' form (matches chapter_blueprint.relationship_turns.dyad). For one-to-group relationships use 'Name/Group' form.

arc_type.description: deepening = grows closer; rupturing = breaks down; reconciling = breaks then mends; transactional = operational only, no emotional change; static = intentionally unchanging for thematic contrast; quiet_alliance = unspoken understanding that holds without declaration, the relationship's shape is held as texture rather than progression.

arc_summary.description: One-sentence description of the arc's shape.

ghost.description: The prior event or wound that defines the relationship's starting state.

lie.description: The unspoken belief the relationship operates on that must be exposed or changed.

want.description: What the relationship pursues on the surface.

need.description: What the relationship actually requires to resolve healthily.

arc_phase_map.description: Chapter-level map of relationship progression. Suggested phases: initial_state, first_strain, deepening_trust or first_crack, breaking_point or mutual_recognition, resolved_state. Values are chapter references.

payoff_chapter.description: Chapter where the relationship reaches its resolved state.

brooks_alignment.description: Larry Brooks's Story Engineering beat map. Optional beats (inciting_incident, first_pinch_point, second_pinch_point, climax) supplement the four-part phase segmentation — use when the beat is distinct from its enclosing phase. Brooks places the inciting incident at ~12%, first pinch at ~37.5%, second pinch at ~62.5%, and climax near the end of part_4_resolution.

inciting_incident.description: Optional. The ~12% beat where the disturbance first meaningfully touches the protagonist, distinct from but preceding the First Plot Point.

first_pinch_point.description: Optional. The ~37.5% beat that reminds the reader of the antagonist force's active threat without advancing the plot skeleton.

second_pinch_point.description: Optional. The ~62.5% beat that escalates antagonist pressure as the protagonist attacks but begins to fail.

climax.description: Optional. The final confrontation beat, typically the last ~10-15% of the book, distinct from the denouement that may follow.

voice_definition.description: Narrative voice identity for the book. Produced by Step 5 of the concept workshop.

reference_authors.description: Authors whose prose the book emulates. Each entry is an object with guidance on what to emulate and what to avoid.

character_voices.description: Per-character voice guidance, keyed by character name. Each value is a free-form description of how the character speaks and thinks.

anti_slop_rules.description: Either a flat list of slop-avoidance rules (Betrayal-style) or a two-tier object separating book-level derived_rules from sentence-level line_level_rules (Ruusan-style). Both shapes are canonical; context_assembler.py renders either into the drafter brief. Replaces the legacy nested anti_slop.{banned_words, banned_phrases} structure.

anti_patterns.description: Structural anti-patterns to avoid (e.g., 'no prophecy fulfillment structure').

force_description_guidelines.description: Optional — genre-specific phenomenological rules for describing magic, the Force, or other setting-specific systems.

info_id.description: Legacy alias for revelation_id. Accepted for backward compatibility.

content.description: Legacy alias for 'what'. Accepted for backward compatibility.

revealed_in.description: Chapter where this is revealed. Accepts integer or string reference.

revealed_chapter.description: Legacy alias for revealed_in (integer only). Accepted for backward compatibility.

items.description: Each entry must supply either 'term' (canonical form) or 'canonical_form' (workshop-style). Both are accepted for compatibility with different workshop outputs.

first_appearance.description: Chapter of first appearance. Accepts either an integer chapter number or a string reference like 'Chapter 1' or 'Chapter 5 (First Plot Point)'.

stress_test_scores.description: 9-dimension stress test scores. Produced by Step 10 of the concept workshop. All scores may be null when scoring has not yet been run or is intentionally deferred (common for draft concepts pre-assessment or between revisions).

subplots.description: Subplot list. Each entry describes a subplot arc with an ID, name, narrative function, summary, and the chapters across which it is active.

hooks.description: Hook list. Each entry describes a narrative hook with an ID, type (hard/soft/series), plant and payoff chapters, and a description of the reader contract.

planted_in.description: Chapter where the hook is planted. Accepts either integer or string form.

resolved_in.description: Chapter where the hook is resolved (or 'next_book' for series hooks).

scene_cards.description: WORKSHOP-ONLY intermediate (marker: workshop_only=true). Produced by Step 8 of the concept workshop and consumed exclusively by the extraction step. The drafting pipeline MUST NOT read this list directly — canonical scene cards live at data/franchises/{franchise}/books/{book}/scene_cards/*.json (matching schemas/scene_card.json) and are the sole source of truth at drafting time. The compliance validator accepts an empty scene_cards array (including zero items) when extracted canonical cards are present for the given franchise/book context. Leaving entries here after extraction is a protocol violation, not a second source of truth.

promise_payoff_ledger.description: High-level reader-promises tracked across the book. Complements the hook map — hooks are plot-mechanic contracts, promises are thematic/character-level reader expectations that may span multiple beats. Populated during Step 7 or as a post-stress-test enrichment.

related_hook_id.description: Optional cross-reference to a hook in the hooks array that shares this promise's reader contract.

quality_overrides.description: Per-project overrides for quality metric thresholds. Prevents franchise-specific false positives (e.g., 'Force' flagged as overused in Star Wars).

word_frequency_allowlist.description: Words that should not be flagged as overused. Case-insensitive.

semantic_similarity_threshold.description: Cosine similarity above which paragraph pairs are flagged. Default: 0.85.

max_similar_pairs_per_1k_words.description: Maximum similar paragraph pairs per 1000 words before triggering alert.

canon_profile.description: Franchise canon and continuity profile for the canon expert agent. All specialization for canon validation comes from this section — the agent code contains zero franchise-specific content.

franchise.description: The franchise or world this story belongs to. Use 'original' for original fiction.

continuity.description: Which continuity or canon tier applies. For original worlds, use 'primary'.

continuity_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the continuity scope — what counts as valid source material and what doesn't.

era_description.description: When this story is set within the franchise timeline, including key context about the state of the world.

narrative_register.description: The expected prose tone and voice — space opera, grimdark medieval, literary fantasy, hard sci-fi, etc.

cross_continuity_violations.description: Specific terms, characters, or concepts from OTHER continuities that should be flagged if they appear.

anachronistic_terms.description: Real-world terms that break the franchise voice, mapped to their in-universe replacements.

meta_reference_rules.description: Out-of-universe reference systems or fan terminology that should never appear in prose.

franchise_terminology_notes.description: Any additional franchise-specific voice or terminology guidance.

extended_metadata.description: Container for project-specific structural data that doesn't belong in the universal schema. Examples: technique_lineage (Star Wars Legends), jacen_parallel, workshop_origin. Arbitrary sub-fields are permitted.
